chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu Ali ibn Ayyub, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Abdullah al-Lahham, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who buys the daughter of a man from the people of shirk (polytheism) and takes her as a slave. He said, 'There is no harm in it.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a Muslim to buy the daughter of a polytheist as a slave?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the acquisition of a polytheist woman as a slave through purchase, reflecting the pre-modern juristic consensus on the status of *ahl al-shirk* in Islamic law. This ruling underscores the legal mechanism by which non-Muslims could enter the Islamic sphere of servitude, distinct from free conversion, and highlights the practical application of *milk al-yamin* (possession of the right hand) in early Shia jurisprudence. The permissibility emphasizes that the primary barrier to marriage was often religious difference, whereas ownership was permissible regardless of the specific type of polytheism.
